title: Intermittent TPS regression during variant probing causes TTFT spikes
creator: Asha Raman
summary: Several enterprise customers reported intermittent First-Token (TTFT) spikes and total tokens/sec drops affecting high-throughput chat endpoints. The spike correlates with dynamic variant probing and quantized-kernel selection when model variants with slightly different context lengths are batched together. Issue appears across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments but is customer- and workload-dependent.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10: On-call observed TTFT increase from 120ms -> 450ms for a small subset of requests to model:llama-2-70b-int8-variants. Spike coincides with sudden drop in token/sec throughput on affected nodes (Grafana dashboard ref below).

2026-03-11: Reproduced locally by replaying customer trace with multiplexed requests that interleave short (<=64) and long (>=1024) contexts. Dynamic batcher merged streams and the kernel selector preferred an int8 fused-kernel with incorrect stride heuristics for those batches.

2026-03-12: Kernel selector logs show fallback to generic GEMM path after OOM-safe-heuristic triggered; however fallback latency dominated path for first token due to repeated kernel rebinds when probing variant metadata changed mid-stream.
2026-03-13: Dedicated environment shows higher incidence due to pinned GPU kernel cache fragmentation; Private installs on older CUDA drivers exhibited similar behavior but less frequent.

Hypothesis: Variant-probing step (warmup check to decide quantized kernel) races with KV-cache priming and causes transient kernel-miss + context-serialization penalty, inflating TTFT and temporarily reducing tokens/sec.
steps_taken: 2026-03-11: Throttled variant probing frequency for affected customers via runtime flag runtime.variant_probe_interval=5s (hot patch) — reduced incidence but did not eliminate spikes.
2026-03-12: Deployed a telemetry patch to emit per-request kernel-selection decisions and kernel-rebind durations (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9273).
2026-03-13: Added temporary per-customer request-shaping policy to smooth bursts from the front-door for the 3 escalated customers (config: kd-shaper:conservative).
2026-03-14: Reproduced end-to-end in staging with synthetic fanout and measured TTFT improvement after probe backoff + single-probe-per-session guard.

2026-03-15: Implemented a pragmatic fallback: if kernel selection path triggers >2 rebinds in 250ms, force a preemptive full-precision kernel path for that session to stabilize TTFT (branch: feature/variant-probe-stabilizer).
fix_plan: Short-term (hotfix): Introduce probe-backoff + session-level probe lock to prevent repeated kernel rebinds. Implemented as runtime flag and feature gated for 24h canary on affected clusters.

Medium-term: Update kernel selector heuristic to account for batch context heterogeneity and prefer stable kernel paths when KV-cache warmup has not completed. Add unit tests and microbenchmarks for mixed-context batches.
Long-term: Add model-variant compatibility metadata to the model catalog so router can avoid cross-variant fanout for high-throughput endpoints unless explicitly allowed by tenant config.
Safety: Add observability to detect probe-induced rebind loops and automated circuit-breaker that disables probing when >0.5% of requests in a minute see rebinds > threshold.
Rollbacks: Hotfix is reversible via feature flag; rollout plan includes immediate rollback criteria tied to error budget and customer impact metrics.
rollout_plan: Canary (now -> 2026-03-16): Enable probe-backoff and session-level probe lock on 5% of host pools serving hosted customers and on 2 test dedicated clusters. Monitor TTFT, tokens/sec, and error rates every 5 minutes.
Stage (2026-03-17): Expand to all hosted clusters and add opt-in for dedicated customers experiencing issues. Notify private customers with recommended config changes for their next patch window.
Full (target 2026-03-18): Flip default probe-backoff on for runtime-1.22. Coordinate with Support to close escalations once stability confirmed for 72h rolling window.
Rollback criteria: >5% increase in 5xxs or >10% degradation in median tokens/sec on canary pools within first 30 minutes.
acceptance_criteria: TTFT median for affected customer endpoints returns to within 10% of baseline for 72h continuous window.
Tokens/sec for end-to-end scenarios recovers to baseline +/-5% under identical synthetic load.
No increase in 5xx or dropped-stream errors attributable to probe-lock changes.
Telemetry shows probe-induced kernel-rebind events reduced to <0.1% of requests across fleets.
Rollout runbook updated and support playbook documented with mitigation steps.
